drugRefs.regimenLabel: Piperacillin-tazobactam or Meropenem (broader if prior resistant organisms/healthcare exposure)
drugRefs.dose: Pip-tazo 4.5 g IV q6-8h or Meropenem 1-2 g IV q8h
drugRefs.why: Maximal reasonable empiric gram-negative and anaerobic coverage is warranted given the mortality risk of inadequate initial coverage in septic shock.
Empiric gram-positive/MRSA coverage is added given the severity of illness and the consequences of missing a resistant gram-positive organism.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Add antifungal (e.g., Fluconazole or Echinocandin) if specific risk factors
drugRefs.coverage: Considered in patients with multiple risk factors for invasive candidiasis (prolonged broad-spectrum antibiotics, central line, TPN, recent abdominal surgery) who remain unstable despite antibacterial therapy.

stewardship.deescalation: Mandatory reassessment at 48-72 hours: narrow to source/organism-directed therapy, discontinue empiric antifungal or vancomycin if not supported by cultures, and target the shortest effective duration once source control is achieved.

framework: Broad empiric coverage is justified in septic shock specifically because of the mortality cost of delay — but this must be paired with mandatory reassessment and de-escalation at 48-72 hours once cultures return.
Do not continue maximal broad-spectrum therapy beyond what culture data supports — septic shock survivors are at high risk of unnecessarily prolonged broad-spectrum exposure if this step is skipped.
Source control (drainage of abscess, removal of infected line/device, debridement) is as important as antibiotics and must be pursued in parallel, not after stabilization.
